that drifts. tests/test_status.py grades it in CI; a separate status renderer merges
it with the items that are not publishable.
Why it exists: a review of this project's own notes on 2026-09-28 found three items describing
their work as 'BUILT, unshipped (commit a4722fb, not pushed; no release cut)' for a change that
had shipped in 1.0.37. Nothing was lying on purpose - the record was prose, and prose has no
way to disagree with the repository. So every item here carries an anchor git can check.

items.title: one run per conversation on every route, and the page's assets hold to what they say
items.detail: /api/chat drives the conversation the body names, registers its run atomically (_web_claim_run under WEB_RUNS_LOCK; simultaneous POSTs get 409), touches the registry; WEB_REGISTRY_MAX=200 aggregate with the shared conversation protected; the runlog appends one line per checkpoint (compaction past WEB_RUNLOG_COMPACT_AT, view-side dedup/caps); downloads honour Range (206/416) and carry RFC 5987 filename*; one _asset helper with mtime/size ETags (304) serves the five asset routes and survives a vanished file; the CSS themes once per (mtime,size) and revalidates; platform-reserved upload names are rewritten and an unwritable name answers 400 instead of dropping the socket; drop_line keeps uids the page holds; out-of-range edits log a warning; web.port 0 probes the recorded port; JSON replies are UTF-8. 27 checks red on the pre-fix snapshot.

items.title: an offline window costs ~1650 process restarts, one every 10s
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (3d6a653), merged to main. The lane start is retried in this process on tinycmdr-supervise.py's own curve and reset rule (5/10/20/40/60s, LANE_BACKOFF_START/MAX/RAPID_EXIT_S pinned to the supervisor's constants by tests/test_lane_health.py, so the two policies cannot drift), for both lanes, with one log line per state change and lane_down() kept accurate so health and logs/state.json stay meaningful. SystemExit passes straight through, so a missing token, a broken config and a token the API refused still exit, and /restart still exits 75. The unit and the plist keep a fixed delay as the CRASH backstop, raised 10 -> 60s, with the reason in each file. Audited and fixed: Measured 2026-09-30 on the Mac: the configured Mattermost host stopped resolving at 00:15:33 and the LAN model endpoint was unreachable with it, so run_bot() raised, main() re-raised by design (tinycmdr.py ~22346), and launchd's KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit: false} with ThrottleInterval 10 respawned the process every ~10s until the network returned at ~05:00:21 - 1654 startups of a 22k-line module, each printing the capabilities banner and one lane-down line. The 'one line per STATE, not per attempt' rule at ~22344 is what kept the log to 1654 lines instead of 1654 times N; it did not stop the restarts. Nothing was lost (jobs.json is empty, so no scheduled work was due), but the window is deterministic for this host rather than bad luck, and it repeats nightly.

items.title: an offline window leaves no record once the lane recovers
items.detail: logs/state.json holds only the CURRENT verdict: after the 2026-09-30 00:15-05:00 outage it reads an empty failures map and a lane that is ok - lane_down() empties the failures map on recovery, so the only trace of 4h45m offline is 1654 lines in logs/launchd.err.log. `tinycmdr health` reports the live state with an exit code, which is the right answer WHILE it is down; an operator who was asleep learns nothing afterwards. The offline window costs more than the chat lane: the model endpoint is on the same LAN, so the agent can do nothing at all for those hours.
items.gate: on the first successful connect after a gap past a threshold, say so where the operator reads (a chat line and/or a field in status/health): the window, and that nothing was missed. While offline no notice is possible at all, so the report has to be the recovery rather than an alert

items.title: Telegram swallows a second chat's message, and can lose a /stop
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (8436501), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. dedupe keyed on (chat_id, message_id); submit() mints the cancel event, the queue item carries it, and the worker adopts it instead of overwriting the slot. Behaviour note: a /stop now also cancels a message already queued behind the live run; each affected run reports stopped, and the slot is popped when the run finishes, so the chat keeps working. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29. self.seen is a flat deque of bare message ids (18333) and handle() drops a repeat unconditionally (18459-18463) - Telegram ids are per-chat, so two allowed users' identical ids collide silently. Separately, submit() pre-creates poller.cancel[chat_id] (18634) and the worker overwrites it with a fresh Event (18576-18582), so a /stop landing in that window is discarded. The document's related clause (a /stop while another task is queued stops the RUNNING one) is normal behaviour, not this bug.

items.title: a hard-wedged run keeps the session lock, so the respawned worker blocks forever
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (f9820ba), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. run() takes the session lock with a deadline (Agent._run_lock_wait_secs, 60s) and on expiry ANSWERS with the /tinycmdr restart force guidance instead of blocking; the wedged run's lock is never touched (a plain Lock has no force-release). Key rotation was the alternative and was rejected: it would hand the backlog a different session. Residual: a second run that legitimately shares the session and runs longer than 60s now fails fast with that message rather than waiting. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED end to end 2026-09-29. run() holds self._lock(session_key) for the whole run (13467); _lock is a bare threading.Lock with no acquire timeout (12404-12405); the abandon path pops active/running and respawns a worker only when the queue is non-empty (17022-17046) and releases nothing, and reset() never pops a lock either. The fresh worker blocks in run() forever, and the message telling the operator it is picking up their queue is false. Two corrections to the finding: the respawn is conditional, and after it new text is STEERED into the dead run (16933-16940) rather than queued, so the operator is never even shown the queued-behind notice. /restart force on the listener thread (16872-16886) is the only real out.

items.title: the 429 retry sleep ignores cancel_event
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (dfc3c55), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. the wait is sliced in 0.25s steps against cancel_event and raises OperatorStop, mirroring _post_watchdog. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29 at 13111-13112 (not 13087). One unconditional time.sleep(wait) in _chat, while _post_watchdog promises a /stop lands within a quarter second (1712). cancel_event is already in scope. Nuance the finding misses: wait comes from the Retry-After header, so it is 0 without one, 60 is a cap, and it happens at most once per call.

items.title: one transient mid-stream break blacklists streaming for the process
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (dfc3c55), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. StreamFailed now carries not_a_stream, and only the no-SSE cause blacklists the URL or clears stream_on. Deliberate reading: the SAME-CALL retry is still sent non-streaming (bounded); what the finding was about - the process-lifetime blacklist and the other endpoints in the call - is fixed. Audited and fixed: PARTIAL 2026-09-29. All four StreamFailed raises (1979 no first byte, 1982 idle gap, 2129 mid-stream break, 2138 no SSE data) reach one handler that adds the URL to the process-global _STREAM_UNSUPPORTED and sets stream_on = False (13054-13058), which also suppresses stream for the remaining failover endpoints in that call. Real, but the finding overstates one consequence: cancel latency is unaffected (the watchdog slices at 0.25 s regardless of streaming); what is lost is live progress display and the socket hang-up that stops a trickling server.

items.title: the locality cache never expires, so the egress gates can be stale
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (dc16cd2), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. the cache stores (verdict, at) and a hit older than WINDOW_TTL (300s) is a miss. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29. _LOCAL_URL_CACHE is read and written with no TTL, eviction or size bound (1288, 1313-1316) and fronts the failover filter (12920, 12929), search and fetch egress (7008, 7087) and the llama.cpp extension decision (2468, 2400). Correction: the trigger is a DNS re-pointing of a HOSTNAME - an IP literal is its own cache key and never re-resolves, so DHCP renumbering of one is inert. Reverse staleness (remote cached, later local) is the harmless direction. WINDOW_TTL = 300 at 1599 is the in-tree precedent.

items.title: a key added after startup is never scrubbed
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (dc16cd2), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. _SECRETS is re-derived at the end of _verb_config, _config_take_effect and run_setup; _env_set was deliberately left alone (giving .env keys to os.environ mid-process would widen what an in-process load_config honours). Audited and fixed: PARTIAL 2026-09-29. _SECRETS = _secret_values() runs once at import (2532) and nothing re-derives it: config set ends at CONFIG.update(back) (20857), model add ends at _config_take_effect (20643-20651), run_setup updates CONFIG (19134) and writes .env through _env_set (21378) without touching os.environ. The finding's named vector is wrong, though: model add takes --key-env NAME only and never an inline key. The real vectors are config set llm.api_key <value> and config set llm.fallbacks with an inline key (both allowed because the secret guard skips the llm section), plus setup keys that only ever reach .env.

items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (f115855), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. os.chmod(run_dir, 0o700) right after the mkdir; the test asserts the mode (a plain mkdir is 0755 under umask 022). items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (b122f6c), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. reset() pops the session's lock when it is not held (a held one is left alone - an abandoned worker may still own it). items.title: the installers never verify the SHA256SUMS they ship beside
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (c92b750), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. install.sh fetches SHA256SUMS, picks this asset's line and refuses a corrupt or truncated transfer before unpacking; no sums file, or one that omits the asset, is refused too, with TINYCMDR_NO_SUMS=1 as the deliberate way past. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29. Neither install.sh nor install/install-tinycmdr.sh mentions SHA256SUMS, sha256 or shasum anywhere, so the curl-into-bash path - the one the README leads with - unpacks whatever arrived while the README's sha256sum -c step stays manual. Releases are unsigned, so the sums only catch corruption or truncation; that is exactly the case the pipe-to-shell path handles worst.

items.title: a zombie batch worker writes into a later turn's results
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (f9820ba), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. the four per-turn buffers ride in as default arguments, so a late worker can only write into its own turn's list. Pinned source-level: the batch deadline is ~440s, so the race cannot be driven in a test; the suite already pins that worker's stop guard the same way. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29, narrower than described. work(i, tc) is a nested def in the same frame as the per-turn buffers (14155-14160) and the for-loop creates no scope, so every turn's closure shares one cell; ex.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) (14299) deliberately lets a hung worker outlive its batch, and cancel_futures only cancels not-yet-started ones. The later list is live only until its own batch completes (roughly its own duration), and the concrete damage is an orphan tool message plus '[HARNESS: no result was recorded for this call...]' padding for the current call (12203, 12240) - with an IndexError if the stale index exceeds the later list's length.

items.title: prompt assembly can write notes.md (and measurement can too)
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (84bbb4f), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. the read path no longer calls curate_notes: it bounds what the PROMPT sees (newest cap chars, with a marker) and leaves the file byte-identical; the write path is unchanged. items.title: a cloud endpoint is driven at an assumed 8k window
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (2f46e9c), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. doctor names the lever for a non-LAN endpoint on an assumed window (llm.max_context_tokens, with the provider's documented window), setup says the same thing where it configures such an endpoint, and config.example.json's window_profiles comment now says a band CAPS character budgets and never widens the window. Kept deliberately: no second log warning (the existing one already names the key), and no window_profiles behaviour change - it cannot widen a window. Residual: a genuinely unreachable non-LAN endpoint now gets the window advice instead of the old did-not-answer line; the wording is neutral about which case it is. Audited and fixed: PARTIAL 2026-09-29. Detection fails on OpenAI-style endpoints (no max_model_len, no /props), so the envelope takes budget=8000, reply=min(cfg_max or 2048, 2048) (12638-12639) - the numbers are right. Two corrections: it is not silent (log.warning 12641 names llm.max_context_tokens, and doctor reports the endpoint as NO ANSWER with a problem, 20532-20535), and the suggested fix is misaimed - window_profiles caps character budgets by detected window band and cannot widen the assumed window; only llm.max_context_tokens can. Side effect worth knowing: the example config's 16384 band then applies small-model character caps to a cloud user.

items.title: the envelope is measured against the primary endpoint and reused on failover
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (f1047ea), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. _endpoint_window caches per server root with a per-entry TTL, _envelope is valid only for the same session AND endpoint, each failover request is sized to the endpoint that gets it (new _fit_payload, which skips the primary so the server prefix cache is untouched), ContextOverflow carries the endpoint that rejected it, and _force_shrink now targets the FAILING endpoint's window. Merged with F-05 and repaired in 03b8bc4: the TTL moved to the monotonic clock, so the two tests that back-dated a cache entry with time.time() had to be moved to now_mono() (they failed in the gate only, which is the semantic half of a merge no textual conflict shows). Audited and fixed: PARTIAL 2026-09-29, and worse than described. _endpoint_window probes CONFIG['llm']['base_url'] only (12545-12557) and the envelope cache is keyed by session (12582-12583), computed once before the endpoint loop (12863, cap at 12955), so a fallback inherits the primary's window, reply and budget. The self-heal is not reliable: _force_shrink targets self._context_budget(key) * 0.5 (12843-12850) - the PRIMARY budget - and the run loop retries once (13711), so 32k primary to 8k fallback can still die after shrinking.

items.title: watchdog, steering and cancel are per-lane, so a new lane inherits none of them
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (390c46f), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. drive_run now opens a session-keyed run record for EVERY run (RunControl/RunRegistry): watchdog activity, a cancel event and a steering queue come by construction. Telegram steers a mid-run message instead of queueing it and its workers exit after an idle wait; the scheduler needed no change at all - drive_run supplies what it lacked. Mattermost keeps its own watchdog (the stronger guard: it also reclaims the wedged worker) and registers watch=False, so nothing is watched twice. Deliberately kept: Mattermost's own active/_stall_tick/_stop_channel. Residual: a watchdog abandon on a channel-less run (Telegram) logs instead of posting, and surfaces through the run's own stopped answer. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED structurally 2026-09-29. Mattermost owns the watchdog registration (active at 16622, _stall_tick 17016), the cancel plumbing (16446, 17175) and steering (17449); Telegram calls drive_run with a cancel_event and no steer_cb (18590), so a mid-run message queues instead of steering - which contradicts README:110 and 137; and the scheduler passes neither (9160-9163). Telegram workers also block on q.get() with no timeout (18564) where Mattermost's exit after 10 s idle (16967-16969). One correction: the CLI lane does have steering and cancel (19806-19814), so 'only Mattermost' should read 'only Mattermost and the CLI'. drive_run consolidated the CALLBACK half only (15764-15765); this is the lifecycle half, and F-04b and F-11 are instances of it.

items.title: a scheduled run has no cancel event and never enters the watchdog
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (390c46f), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. closed by F-06 - a scheduled run now has a cancel event and a watchdog record, so a channel /stop reaches it. Scheduler._fire was not touched: it already passes a channel id, and drive_run now supplies the rest. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29, harm overstated. Scheduler._fire calls drive_run with no cancel_event and no steer_cb (9160-9163) and never touches dispatcher.active (set only at 16622), so _stall_tick never sees the run and a channel /stop finds nothing (17173-17177). Correction: manifest drop-in tools ARE bounded by their own per-call timeout (10144-10168 through run_capture's deadline, 4513-4531); what is unbounded is a native in-process drop-in (10059-10061) or any other in-process hang, because max_minutes is only tested at turn boundaries (13585, 13876, 13926, 14031, 14495).
items.gate: done - merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch; maintenance/ledger-tag.py states the release claim on this anchor when the tag exists

items.title: every duration is wall-clock, so a suspend abandons healthy runs
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (ad6562a), merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch. now_mono()/now_wall() helpers; every ELAPSED calculation moved to monotonic - the stall watchdog and its records, the run budget, _post_watchdog, run_capture, the ask wait, the window/envelope TTLs, the new RunRegistry. Cron fire times, persisted/displayed timestamps and last_seen stay wall-clock, and test_catchup (which pins that) stays green. Falsified before/after: the old code abandoned a healthy run after a simulated 30-minute suspend (wall +1800s, monotonic frozen) and never reached the budget after a backward wall step; the fixed code does neither. Audited and fixed: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29, severity re-scoped. Counts exact: 102 time.time() calls by grep, zero monotonic or perf_counter. Deadlines really are wall clock - _post_watchdog (1707-1723), run_capture (4513-4529), ask waits (9397-9400), WINDOW_TTL (1599 against 1431, 12553, 12581), the run budget (13589 vs 13876/13926/14031/14495) - and _stall_tick's quiet is now minus a wall-clock last (17020-17023, last touched at 16558/16622). But the practical arm is not NTP stepping (slewed, corrected in seconds): it is suspend/resume on this laptop, where one 30-minute sleep makes every active run look wedged and gets it abandoned and cancelled. The fix is a per-site audit, not a helper swap - cron fire times (9100, 9061-9062) and persisted or displayed timestamps (state.json at, last_seen) must stay wall-clock, and test_catchup actively pins that.
items.gate: done - merged to main in the 1.0.41 batch; maintenance/ledger-tag.py states the release claim on this anchor when the tag exists

items.title: zip-slip in update <zip> (refuted)
items.detail: REFUTED 2026-09-29. The code fact is true - z.extractall(work) with no filter kwarg (20922-20924) - but the security claim is not, and the suggested fix would not run. zipfile.ZipFile.extractall has no filter parameter in the supported 3.10-3.12 band (signature on this box's 3.12.13: (self, path=None, members=None, pwd=None); filter= is a tarfile/3.12 PEP 706 name), and CPython's _extract_member strips leading separators and every '..' component before joining. Proved here: an archive carrying ../escaped.txt, /abs.txt and ..\..\backslash.txt extracted entirely inside the target directory. Residual is cosmetic: CPython silently sanitises rather than refusing. No action; recorded so it is not re-reported as a vulnerability.
items.gate: done - refuted; only an optional hygiene pass (reject such members) remains, and only if a future Python version changes the behaviour

items.title: a streamed markdown answer rendered three times, one of them truncated mid-word
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (8abdb49). Reproduced before the fix: streaming an answer containing a markdown table drew a dim whitespace-collapsed pipe line, an 'answer' card made from that draft (flattened pipes, truncated at checkin_note_chars with a trailing ellipsis), and the rendered card. RunReporter.narration collapses whitespace and caps at 400 chars; CliDestination.drop() drew a card from that text; and the console loop's dedupe (answer.startswith(shown), shown.startswith(answer)) can never match an intact answer against the mangled draft. drop() now only records the draft, for the plain path's single-print, and the console loop draws the whole answer exactly once whenever a screen exists. tests/test_tui.py reproduces the table case and asserts one answer card, no flattened copy on the screen and no truncation glyph.
items.gate: merged to main (gate 68/68 green); release.sh states the tagged claim; maintenance/ledger-tag.py states the release claim on this anchor when the next tag exists

items.title: colours lived per kind, and the answer's frame was ANSI blue (purple on a dark theme)
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (8abdb49). TUI_KINDS carried a literal colour per kind and cli_banner() hardcoded border_style="blue"; rich's named blue is ANSI 4, which dark themes render blue-violet, and the reviewer's own screenshot showed the answer frame as purple while the answer, the tool lines and the narration all competed for the eye. There is now one TUI_PALETTE table (accent #5fbfbf / cyan, result #5fbf7f / green, failure red bold, question magenta bold, answer frame bright_black, ambient dim) and one tui_colour_tier() that picks truecolor/256/16/none once per process from COLORTERM, TERM, WT_SESSION, with NO_COLOR winning and TINYCMDR_COLOR forcing a tier for a screenshot or a test. TUI_KINDS names a ROLE, so a lane or a kind cannot fork the palette again. tests/test_tui.py grades all four tiers by their SGR bytes and asserts no tier paints anything blue.
items.gate: merged to main (gate 68/68 green); release.sh states the tagged claim; the next tag carries it

items.title: the console had no full-screen mode, so a live draft could never be replaced
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-29 (8abdb49). `tinycmdr --app` is the same session in an alternate-screen app: header with model/endpoint/context, a repaintable transcript pane, a status bar, an always-focused input and key hints. No port, no server and no browser (the removed web lane stays removed) and no new dependency - prompt_toolkit already owns smcup/rmcup and the Windows console glue. AppScreen is a TuiScreen subclass, so the palette and the cards are the same code; the streamed draft is one item the answer card REPLACES, which is what makes the three-render defect unreachable there. The console loop runs in a worker thread (the app owns the main thread) and stdout is swapped so the banner, /help and /status become transcript lines; on exit the terminal is restored and the session's last answer is reprinted inline. tests/test_tui.py drives the real Application headlessly (key pipe, dummy output) and asserts one answer card, the draft replaced rather than stacked, no stats in the transcript, /exit leaving both, and no NETWORK socket opened during the run.
items.gate: merged to main (gate 68/68 green); release.sh states the tagged claim. The reviewer still has to look at it on macOS/Linux/Windows terminals (the brief's platform matrix) before it is called shipped

items.title: a tool call and its result are two boxes where one visual unit would read better
items.detail: The brief's section 6 target state, deferred on its own instruction ('if this proves too invasive in v1, defer it') because T-01/T-02/T-03 outranked it. Today a call is one box and its result a second box stacked with no gap; the target is the call box with its result appended as a dim footer line ('check name, 0.2s') inside or immediately under the same frame, expanding to a separate box only on failure or when the output preview exceeds one line. The inline screen would have to hold the call's renderable and amend it, which the append-only inline path cannot do - so this is a natural follow-on for --app (where the transcript is repainted) and then, if it earns it, for the inline screen.
items.gate: the call and its result read as one visual unit in the transcript; on failure and on long output still two, with tests/test_tui.py's rhythm checks updated to the new shape

items.title: a streamed narration line stair-stepped: one row per delta, never growing
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (44f97d1), found by the round-2 review and reproduced from the bytes. CliDestination._write routes painted text to the screen's raw_ansi, which called print_formatted_text - and that appends a newline per call by default, so a sentence arriving in three deltas landed on three ragged rows instead of growing in one; the old `if text.strip()` guard on the same path also silently dropped the newline that ends the line, so nothing ever closed it. Open-line writes now pass end="" and flush, and the close writes one real newline. tests/test_tui.py renders a three-delta stream and asserts one line with exactly one newline.

items.title: the draft-pulse threshold ran on text already printed, so the prose before a pipe stayed on screen
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (44f97d1). T-02's pulse was gated on a property of text the terminal had ALREADY been given, so any page that turned into a table mid-stream left its opening prose behind for good ('... The' / '... The only Apple machine that hits 800+ GB/s is the **M4 Ultra** - ...' in the round-2 review) - and an inline terminal cannot unprint. The opening of each line (200 characters or 1.5 s, whichever comes first) is now buffered and the decision is made before the first character lands: short chatter commits as prose, a long or structured draft commits as the single dim pulse. Dim previews also drop markdown emphasis; the answer text is never touched. Reviewing this found a gap of its own - a held line interrupted by a tool call was never drawn - so anything about to print commits the hold first, and tests/test_tui.py pins both cases.

items.title: the full-screen mode looked like the same cards in a frame, and the human door still opened the inline lane
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (44f97d1), after the first --app screenshot ('looks the exact same') and the round-3 review. The app is now a window: a frame whose title bar carries the app name, the session and a live clock; a left rail with the session, a context gauge, the last run's calls/tok-s, the model and the keys; cards drawn on a filled surface; a status bar whose spinner and clock tick while a run is in flight; and a labeled `you` composer box. The round-3 items are in the same commit: the transcript opens on the first exchange (the chrome carries the banner, the note and the capability line), an empty draft card is never committed as a stub, the done line and the rail read one run accumulator, no rich Markdown default colour reaches an answer body (magenta headings, cyan lists/table headers and the white `bw` code background were all on screen), the footer carries the run status only, and the input box says `you`. A bare `tinycmdr` now passes --app from both shims on every OS (falling back to inline cards where the app cannot run), and TINYCMDR_APP=1 does the same for a hand-typed --cli. tests/test_tui.py pins the chrome and the six polish behaviours.

items.title: the app filed the model's pre-answer narration above the answer card
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (437f231), the round-4 residual of P-02. Reproduced from the reporter's own call pattern: RunReporter.narration draws a NEW line (CliDestination.line('narration', ...)) and only then streams deltas into it with update(), so the first draw is a committed transcript item and the deltas are a second. The answer card dropped only the item it believed was the draft, so the model's opening sentence stayed filed above the card with its markdown characters intact - literally the last survivor of the triple-render family the brief opened with. AppScreen now tracks the run's draft region (narration lines and streamed deltas since the last real card) and the answer drops the whole span; a card in between ends the region, so narration a tool call came after stays as history. tests/test_tui.py replays the first-draw-plus-deltas shape and asserts no item mentioning the draft survives the card.
items.gate: merged to main (gate 68/68 green); release.sh states the tagged claim for this batch

items.title: an answer card carried a two-row blank band around a markdown table
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (437f231). T-05 again, and the first pass could not have closed it: the band is emitted by the RENDERER, not present in the markup, so stripping blank source lines and collapsing triple newlines left two blank rows between a table and the following paragraph and one before the card's closing border. Measured: 2 rows between the table and a paragraph, 1 row when the answer ended in a table. The answer body now renders through a small renderable that draws the markdown at whatever width the panel gives it (so the wrapping is still rich's own), drops the whole blank run after a table, collapses blank runs elsewhere to one, keeps blank lines inside a code surface (a background style is the giveaway) and crops a line wider than the box - rich's horizontal rule was overflowing by the panel's padding and wrapping onto a second row. tests/test_tui.py asserts a table followed by a paragraph leaves no blank row inside the card.
items.gate: merged to main (gate 68/68 green); release.sh states the tagged claim for this batch

items.title: a pasted page was invisible in the composer: one row, no size, no review
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (437f231), after a question about pasting large text. The data path measured clean before any change - bracketed paste (which the app enables) delivers a paste as one event, so 1 KB / 20 KB / 200 KB all arrived complete in the buffer in about 0.1 s, kept their newlines, never triggered a submit mid-paste, and were handed to the loop as ONE request (only the outer whitespace is stripped) - but the composer showed a single horizontally-scrolled row with nothing anywhere reporting the size, so a page could be sent unreviewed. The box is multiline now, its label reports the size and the keys ('you - 12,345 chars - send, Ctrl-J newline'), it grows to six wrapped rows and collapses when sent, Enter sends and Ctrl-J inserts a newline. tests/test_tui.py pins the label and the growth.
items.gate: merged to main (gate 68/68 green); release.sh states the tagged claim for this batch

items.title: the app advertised scroll keys nothing was bound to, and a wheel that only worked on Windows
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (4daa918), merged to main, after 1.0.44 shipped the app's pane could not be scrolled back up - and the app owns an alternate screen, so the terminal's own scrollback is not there while it runs, which makes the app's own keys the way back up. Two of the three were dead. (1) The rail said '↑↓ PgUp/PgDn scroll' while ↑ and ↓ were bound to NOTHING: only the page keys moved the pane. (2) The wheel did nothing on macOS or Linux even with capture on, because prompt_toolkit's Keys.ScrollUp comes from the Win32 driver alone and a POSIX terminal delivers the wheel as a mouse event at a coordinate, which prompt_toolkit hands to the CONTROL under the pointer - so the app's two `<scroll-up>` bindings could never fire there. Measured in a headless Application driven by a key pipe with capture on: the event landed in the rail's cell and the pane never moved, while the same bytes at the body's coordinates did nothing either. Now: ↑/↓ move one line, FILTERED on an empty composer so the arrows stay the caret for a multi-line paste; Ctrl-Home/Ctrl-End are named in the rail; both panes answer the wheel themselves (three lines a notch); and page scroll, line scroll and Ctrl-Home share _scroll_to(), which clamps to the tail, so _top cannot point past the end. Capture stays off by default (native selection and copy without a modifier key) and the rail says what turning it on buys. Pinned in tests/test_tui.py by driving the real Application with a key pipe and real mouse bytes - every check that existed called scroll() DIRECTLY, which is exactly why a key bound to nothing and a wheel that never fired both read as covered. Residual: with capture off the terminal sends no mouse bytes at all, so the wheel stays opt-in; want it by default, start with TINYCMDR_APP_MOUSE=1.
items.gate: done - merged to main; the README documents the keys; release.sh states the tagged claim on this anchor when the next tag exists

items.title: test_plan's staleness fixture was a literal date, so the suite went red by itself
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (97e9346), merged to main. The ledger-staleness check built its fixture around 'updated': '2026-09-26 15:48' and then demanded the literal '(3d, stale)', so the check graded the calendar rather than the rule: at 15:48 on 2026-09-30 the age became four days and it went red - permanently, on every host, forever. Measured: this tree was green in CI at 13:45Z and red at 21:21Z the same day (run 36778872020, both platforms), and the red is the one that started the failed-run mail. The stamp is now computed 74h back from now - tests/test_ledger.py's idiom for the same claim ('30 * 3600' against '(1d') - and the two hours over three days absorb both the truncation to the minute and a DST step, so the rendered age is '(3d' in any zone on any day; verified in UTC+14, UTC-11 and this host's own. Nuance: run_all.py the red read as a crash: 'died before its own summary: no count line' - that parser gap is its own item (runall-misreads-check-suites).
items.gate: done - merged to main; maintenance/ledger-tag.py states the release claim on this anchor when the next tag exists

items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (66abc30, extended in 2037f12), merged to main. run_all.py's _check_tail() recognised one spelling of a suite's summary, 'N passed, M failed', and annotated every other red '[died before its own summary: no count line]' - which says the suite aborted mid-run and left checks ungraded. items.title: the app's context-gauge check graded this box's session history, not the chrome
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (391bd1a), merged to main, found while answering 'is everything green?'. The check '--app draws a rail with a live context gauge' asserted a filled cell, and the fill is read from the LIVE session (AGENT.stats) and the detected window - so on a clean clone, which is exactly what CI grades, usage is zero, the bar is all shade and the check is red, while the same tree was green here because this box had run a session (7.7K of 110.1K). Measured: red on macOS and Ubuntu from its first full CI run (36782281132, 36784022014) and green here; reproduced by running the suite in a clone of HEAD. The two numbers the gauge reads are pinned for the check and restored afterwards, so the fill is graded as arithmetic (4.1K / 8.2K -> half the bar, the other half shade) with a second arm for a session with no usage, and the rail's fixed 26 columns are pinned too (a longer line is silently cut, never wrapped). items.title: there was no way to get a card's own text out of the app
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (b42553c), merged to main: each transcript item (answer, call, result) should be individually copyable. Native selection could not do it: the pane paints frames (box drawing, wrap points, the rail beside them) and the alternate screen has no scrollback, so what a terminal can select is not what a reader wants to paste. Ctrl-Y now copies the newest transcript item as its own text - the answer's markdown before the renderer touched it, a tool call, a tool result, a question - and pressing it again walks back one item per press, with the status line naming what landed and where it sits ('copied answer 3/9 - 39 chars, pbcopy + OSC 52 + file:...'); any new item resets the walk; Ctrl-B copies the whole transcript in order. The raw text rides with the item that drew it (_draw/_put/_panel/_card carry it down from card(kind, text)) rather than being re-derived from the painted frame, and consecutive printed lines (help, status, /tinycmdr tools) coalesce into ONE item, so a command's output is one step of the walk. Delivery tries every door the host has, because each fails somewhere: the host's own tool (pbcopy / clip.exe / wl-copy / xclip / xsel, the first installed), the terminal over OSC 52 (the only clipboard reachable with no helper, and it travels over ssh - but Terminal.app and tmux without set-clipboard on ignore it silently), and COPY_FILE (gettempdir()/tinycmdr-copy.txt, 0600), which always lands and is named in the status line. items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (c0cc99f), merged to main. The shell runs `run_model_pick()` as its own Application - only a lane that OWNS the terminal may call it, so the inline console's reader thread and `--app` never do. ENTER on a filter that matches nothing does nothing (ESC leaves), any new item cancels a copy walk, and a pipe (a script, a cron job, CI) still gets the plain list it greps. `model add <url>` with several advertised ids and `run_setup`'s model step use the same list, and the setup wizard refuses to run inside `--app`, where its raw input() competes with the app's input box. items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (c0cc99f), merged to main: the installer should probe the endpoint for reachability before continuing. items.title: in --app an answer card said nothing about what it was answering
items.detail: Fixed 2026-09-30 (6ade905), merged to main: the answer card should show the question it answers, the way a reply does. The gap was the app: the composer clears when it sends, so the request was NOWHERE on the transcript - it held cards and nothing else - and the answer card said nothing about what it answered (measured on a pty; the inline `you>` prompt line and the chat message both already show it, which is why only the console lanes change). A dim card of a new kind, `reply`, is filed immediately above the answer card: "re: <your question>", flattened to ONE line and capped at 100 chars with the screen's own ellipsis, because an app pane does not wrap - an uncapped pasted page would be cut mid-word with no marker and push the answer out of the pane. It is an ordinary transcript item, so Ctrl-Y copies it: the question itself became copyable, which the copy walk could not reach before (it walks items, and the question was not one). The ordering is the trick: the model streams a narration draft into the pane and the answer card is what replaces it, so filing the reference before that drop put it INSIDE the region and the drop deleted the reference along with the draft (found by the suite's own T-01 check: one answer card, no stacked draft). AppScreen.answer_card() drops the draft FIRST, then files the reference and the answer; TuiScreen's version is the plain order and `_draw_answer()` is the one entry both console lanes call - including `--once`, whose argv prompt was never on screen either. Pinned in tests/test_tui.py: one capped, flattened line; no reference for an empty question; the screen's own ellipsis when the terminal is not ascii-only; the card filed before the answer is the question; and the reference is copyable.

items.detail: Each endpoint's answer is kept for WINDOW_TTL (300s); a probe that came back EMPTY (a busy llama.cpp box timing out one GET) was cached as 0 for the whole TTL, so every call in that window took the assumed branch - budget 8000 + static + reply = 14,205 tokens with a 4157-token prompt, 17,680 with a 7632-token one - against a server serving 131,072. That guess MOVED with the prompt, which is why it read as unexplainable. An empty answer now expires in WINDOW_MISS_TTL (20s) and is re-asked; a route that RAISED is retried once inside the probe.

items.title: one update command, from any version
items.detail: The rule (docs/development.md + README): every user, on every released version, types /tinycmdr update in chat or `tinycmdr update` in a terminal and it works. The command fetches the latest release package and SHA256SUMS, verifies the download BEFORE touching the install, applies it leaving every host-owned path alone, and never shells out to git (a dirty/pruned/gitless checkout is not a blocker). It is reachable from chat (_CHAT_VERB_SET), runs in an interactive session instead of printing a hint, and a chat update that changed the version RESTARTS onto it. tests/test_verbs.py pins the verb, the published updaters, the release attachments, the launcher fallbacks and the restart; tests/test_tinycmdr_prefix.py grades the door with the verb stubbed.

items.title: update.sh / update.ps1 ship with every release
items.detail: A version-independent updater attached beside install.sh/install.ps1 (and listed in SHA256SUMS): fetch the package for this host, verify it, extract, copy over the install while skipping the host-owned set, print the version it moved from and to. It is what repairs an install whose own updater is missing, broken or git-based. Proven end to end on a real 1.0.44 install planted on a Windows host: 27 files written, 1.0.44 -> 1.0.64, config.json / tools/mine.py / theme.toml / notes.md byte-identical.

When the probe fails, the launcher fetches and runs the published updater. items.title: the harness's memory is an OKF bundle, and the notes.md write path is gone
items.detail: 2026-10-04 brief: redesign the memory system to work off Google Cloud's Open Knowledge Format. Landed: memory/ holds one markdown concept per durable fact with YAML frontmatter (type, title, description, tags; provenance via sources; trust via generated/verified and a derived tier; lifecycle via status/stale_after), plus index.md and log.md; ONE `memory` tool (add, update, deprecate, forget, read, search, list) under one lock, so the concept, the index and the log move together; volatile_context carries the capped, flagged index and never the concepts; notes.md stays on disk and in the prompt, read-only (no migration - a deliberate call); the curator, the archive and the authored-hash sidecar are deleted with their five write-time config keys; attestation (type: Attested Computation) is reserved for a later phase. Rent: the schema declares six fields so the all-revealed worst case is 5,386 est against the 5,400 ratchet, while the default static state is ~4.3K est. tests/test_memory_okf.py (52 checks) pins the format contract; the authorship-guard suite retired with its subject.

items.title: the wizard asks the link before its key, the window at the endpoint, and the page stops prompting when the cookie authenticates

And in mattermost it shows as a normal table' - the page had NO markdown renderer; it renders now (DOM nodes, never innerHTML: tables, fences, lists, emphasis, links, bare URLs, images as links) and Telegram's tg_html grew the same class (it converted only backticks; now the HTML subset, code protected, tables in <pre>). (2) a request that search reach inside conversations, not just the parent session - the rail's box filtered titles only; /api/search?q= reads the model tool's own corpus (session_search_hits()) and the matches render with title, snippet and a click that opens the conversation. (4) 'the harness keeps allowing the model to stop... items.title: the interactive installer's questions, reworked as one flow
items.detail: rework what the installer asks and how. Plan agreed: ONE question set, three doors. The questions live as a table (id, one-line WHY, default, valid answers, where the answer lands: config key/.env) rendered by the Windows installer, the POSIX installer and `tinycmdr setup`; a parity test (the test_installer_parity.py pattern) reads all three and fails when a question id, order or wording drifts, so the set cannot fork. UX rules: one decision per prompt with the WHY on the line above; numbered choices with a visible default whenever there is more than one real answer; bare y/N only for true/false (autostart, fallback consent); ask only what a chosen kind needs (URL for a search API, a key only if that provider has one, blank = anonymous; local model endpoints need no key); never ask what is derivable (egress follows from the search chain, the bot name from the host, the model id from the endpoint probe); re-runs ask once 'Keep the existing configuration?' and then only what changes; the closing summary names every decision back, the files written (.env, config.json) and the single next command; every question keeps a flag/env twin so the fleet push and -NoPause paths stay non-interactive. Order of work: freeze the table and wording for review -> Windows door -> POSIX door -> `setup` -> update the fixed answer sequences in tests/test_setup.py, tests/test_model_setup.py and tests/test_installer_*.py -> one release. The search ask inside this set follows search-provider-declared-next (URL + optional key, repeatable, order = primary then fallbacks). One concrete correction in the same pass: the 'How should you talk to it?' multi-pick offers Mattermost / Telegram / 'sessions by hand' and never mentions the web page, though the page is the DEFAULT door now (bare tinycmdr serves it). The lane menu becomes: 1) the web page (default; token-gated, this machine or your network) 2) Mattermost 3) Telegram - the page's bind, port and token asked only when it is chosen, and terminal sessions (--cli / --once) described as always available instead of offered as a lane to install. The flag twins (-NoWeb, -WebHost, -WebPort, -WebToken) keep the non-interactive path working. Landed in 93dfa82 (dev): the update verb's .git-checkout notice and the dev-kit keep note are gone - policy stays silent - and the host-default note prints only when the package actually moved that default, as one action line (tests/test_update_notes.py fails on the pre-fix build). The rule for the whole pass: update/install output is what changed plus what the operator must do - no internal policy, no history, no process narration. Also removed CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (5e205a3): Contributor Covenant boilerplate that promised enforcement by 'community leaders' for a project I maintain alone, and nothing referenced it; CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md stay.

The wire contract is open: a JSON POST of {query, max_results} (the key as Authorization: Bearer; a 405 retries as searxng's GET ?q=&format=json) answered with a results list, so a search API this build has never heard of needs a url, not a code change - anysearch and searxng keep their exact adapters when their kind is named. `tinycmdr search` lists every entry's state, `search test` runs one query through the chain, and `search allow` is the egress door the BLOCKED line names.

items.title: the verb log never carries a secret value
items.detail: run 9 (fixed 2026-10-06, 0ae0f59). The verb line is logged before dispatch, so `config set mattermost.token hunter2` put the value in tinycmdr.log in cleartext even though the write itself was refused ('put it in.env instead'). _secret_config_path is now one predicate shared by the refusal and the log scrub; the value logs as <redacted>. tests/test_verbs.py: +1 sentinel check, red on the pre-fix build.

items.title: a case-flipped config key gets a near-miss hint
items.detail: run 9 (fixed 2026-10-06, d568caf). Verbs are case-insensitive but keys are not, and `get AGENT.max_steps` answered (not set) rc=0 - silence that reads as 'no such setting'. items.title: a read past the end names the file's length
items.detail: run 9 (fixed 2026-10-06, 7154ff0). An offset past EOF printed the phantom range (lines 99999-99999 of 98) with an empty body; it now returns the honest error naming the file's line count and the largest usable offset, while the last real line still reads. tests/test_read_window.py: +2 checks, red on the pre-fix build (the suite also honors TINYCMDR_SRC now).

items.title: Cannot blank a config value: refuted on this build
items.detail: Refuted 2026-10-06. Verified against this build in a staged tree: `config set zz.e1 "" --str` returns rc=0 and stores the empty string. The audit's rc=2 came from 1.0.80 through a shell (PowerShell strips the empty argument) and the same run's Dismissed list already names that artifact; the probe's 1.0.81 rc=0 measurement matches. items.detail: run 9 (fixed 2026-10-06, 9460a3b). The audit measured 'max_results=0 returns 1 hit'; reproduced here as 0 falling through `or 50` and searching anyway (the audit's tree had one match). items.title: the never tier reads tokens, not one spelling
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (963beae): The never tier was anchored to one surface shape per command: `format /FS:NTFS Q:`, `powershell -enc "..."` and `dd of="/dev/sdz9"` executed with no gate (a switch between verb and target missed an order-anchored regex; the quote erasure removed the quoted operand), and the mkfs read-only exemption was per-line, so `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb # cat` passed. The built-in tier is decided on the tokens of each command segment now - quotes consumed, separators split, redirects and comments read - with the read-only exemption per command. tests/test_guard_battery.py: 16 blocked spellings, 5 allowed mentions, red on the pre-fix build.

items.title: the confirm tier reads the aliases
items.detail: run 10 (fixed 2026-10-06, 963beae). The recursive-delete pattern named `remove-item`, so `ri -Recurse -Force`, `del /s /q`, `erase /s /q` and `rmdir /s /q` matched nothing and ran with no question. The command word is read off tokens, so every alias and flag order lands on the same rule. tests/test_guard_battery.py pins five spellings.

items.title: the gate helpers coerce instead of raising
items.detail: run 10 (fixed 2026-10-06, 963beae). is_blocked(None) coerced while est_tokens(None), cap_output(name, None), _one_json_object(None), _host_is_local(None) and _confirm_hit(None) raised TypeError/AttributeError. items.title: a file log that cannot write must say so
items.detail: run 10: NOT reproduced on macOS (the verb line IS written there, value redacted), but the target box is Windows and the shape has two Windows-specific mechanisms worth keeping this open for: a rollover RENAMES the log and an open handle (the running bot holds tinycmdr.log) makes the rename fail, and the QueueListener thread reports nothing when a handler raises. Both are now visible instead of silent: _LoudRotatingFileHandler falls back to a plain append when the rollover is blocked (losing the rotation is fine, losing the record is not) and writes one stderr line naming the file and the error (2026-10-06, tests/test_file_log.py). To settle it on that box: run a refused verb and look for the WARNING line, then compare tinycmdr.log against tinycmdr.log.1 - the dropped line may be in the predecessor.

items.title: the Responses API is a wire, not a renamed field
items.detail: 2026-10-06. `base_url` pointing at /responses used to send a chat-shaped body; the wire is real now - input items with typed parts, instructions, flat tool schemas, reasoning summaries read into reasoning_content, usage.input_tokens/output_tokens mapped onto the accounting, and a stream adapter feeding the existing SSE reader. An OpenAI-style 400 naming BOTH tools and reasoning_effort escalates once to the /responses sibling and the fact is remembered per endpoint (wire=responses), with the reasoning-field drop kept as the fallback when no sibling exists. tests/test_responses_wire.py: 40 checks, all red pre-fix; a stub-server smoke drove the escalation end to end.

items.title: a patch keeps every byte it did not touch
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (cfd56d6): tools/patch.py decoded with errors="replace" and wrote UTF-8, so a Latin-1/CP1252 source lost every non-ASCII byte to U+FFFD - silently, under a diff that showed only the intended line (caf\xe9 became caf\xef\xbf\xbd). Lossless decode (UTF-8 strict, else Latin-1, byte-transparent) + strict re-encode in the SAME encoding; a character that encoding cannot carry is refused by name. tests/test_patch_bytes.py: 4 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: spill ids are never reused
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (1e9960b): With every spill file deleted the id counter restarted at 1 while the index still carried the old id-1 row, so `spill#1` in a prompt resolved to a different tool's output (measured: two index rows with id==1). The counter advances over every row ever written (file or no file) and the index merge no longer re-persists a row whose file is gone. tests/test_spill_durability.py: 2 checks red pre-fix; simulate_restart now resets the counter, which is what made the bug invisible to the suite before.

items.title: the MCP client validates, remembers failures and reads its server
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (2f0af5a): A non-map agent.mcp_servers answers an ERROR naming the accepted {command, args?} shape instead of raising; a non-numeric mcp_timeout falls back to 60 with one WARNING and a real 0 stays 0; a failed handshake is remembered on the live entry for a bounded 60s window; a dead server is noticed by polling inside the wait; a spec with no command says exactly that; a JSON-string arguments is parsed; tool names match case-insensitively and go out under the server's spelling; stderr is captured into a bounded 20-line/4KB ring and its tail rides every failure; mismatched replies are parked and server-initiated requests are never consumed as replies. tests/test_mcp.py: 50 checks, 24 red pre-fix.

items.title: the Windows helper holds Alt
items.detail: run 11 (fixed 2026-10-06, d6c448b). Python canonicalises Alt to `option` while the PowerShell helper switched only on `alt`, so every Alt combo went out on Windows without Alt held; blocked_combo('f4', ['alt']) slipped the table while the option spelling was refused; and the Windows-only ctrl+alt+delete entry sat behind the macOS keycode gate. Both sides fold alt->option now, the block is decided before the keycode gate, and the helper arms option in all three switches - pinned by a contract check that every modifier the Python half can emit is an arm in the embedded helper. tests/test_computer_use.py: 2 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: the OKF bundle validates at the door and keeps its provenance
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (e912978): `verified:` reads a bare string as {by}; a caller description is bounded at 160 like the generated one; tags take one string or a list and refuse the rest; `update` refuses a title another concept holds; memory/log.md rotates at 64 KB with one predecessor; an unknown `type` is refused by name; load_config never replaces a shipped dict with a non-dict from the file; stale_after must be an ISO instant at write time; update/set_status keep `generated` and record `touched` instead of re-dating the fact. tests/test_memory_okf.py: 33 checks red pre-fix (120/0 after).

items.title: jobs lock and answer honestly; patch keeps every line's ending
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (5e304e5): tools/process.py: `output` reads through read_job_log() (handle closed, __EXIT__ marker stripped), `start` validates command, an unknown action names the vocabulary, wait_for is validated up front, `kill` says exactly what it confirmed (the wrapper gone), and id allocation + table saves run under one file lock (6 concurrent starts in 6 processes now get 6 distinct ids). tools/patch.py: every existing line keeps its own newline (splice-only rewrite; inserted lines take the dominant one), and a whitespace-only or blank-only anchor is refused. tests/test_job_control.py + tests/test_patch_bytes.py: 22 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: the request builder survives a typo, and the tools do what they say
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (e2051ad): reveal_ttl_secs is guarded like mcp_timeout (a typo no longer takes the request builder down; a real 0 means never decay); reveal_tools reads a bare string as one name and refuses other non-lists by name; _tool_category coerces like _tool_blurb; the three pairing repairers skip a non-dict entry without spinning; truncate_middle refuses or cuts honestly at limit 0/1; _spill_signal counts its [HARNESS:...] wrapper against the budget; the stripper scans bracket depth so a nested note does not eat real output; find_tools honours name/topic/action (read name=X answers that tool's blurb and schema, revealing it); create_tool validates the action vocabulary before the arguments. 31 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: computer_use: the typed-text guard sees Windows, and nothing leaks or hangs
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (92e6d19): blocked_text gained the Windows arm (del <drive:>, Remove-Item -Recurse/-Force, format <drive:>, shutdown) and lost its end anchor (`rm -rf / --no-preserve-root`, `rm -rf /; echo hi` blocked now); a dropped window_id on non-macOS is named; Windows depth=0 means 0 levels; _clamp survives 1e999; prune_shots(0) prunes; `cmd+-` is the minus key; the helper's stdout parses from the LAST JSON object; a timeout kills the child tree; the UIA-invoke path goes through _finish. tests/test_computer_use.py: 19 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: emoji cost, the secret vocabulary, and the config-side guard
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (30a51fe): est_tokens gives emoji their own class (~2 tokens each; 400 emoji was 307); the config-side secret rule shares the env-side vocabulary (db.password refused, its value never reaches the verb log); scrub redacts percent-encoded secrets (a URL query no longer leaks one; a case-insensitive pass is deliberately not done); create_tool refuses a name an existing custom tool holds; tools_dir_verdict() answers without an argument. one refuted here by measurement (the spill note's omitted-byte arithmetic agrees across CRLF/accent/3001-byte bodies). tests/test_spill.py, test_scrub.py, test_tool_discovery.py: 13 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: the Telegram lane can ask, and its answers arrive whole
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (cef08fe): TelegramDestination sets has_human (the lane had never asked anything: every confirm-tier command was declined silently, with no line); the confirm question posts with its command as <pre>; run_telegram passes ask_door so ask_user reaches a person; a button answer lands as the option's WORDS; a /stop with a question open stops the run; a second question while one is open is refused; a failed post returns at once (was 30.005s); the caller's wait is capped; the renderer splits first and escapes per chunk (no more tag cut at 4096) and protects fenced blocks; the client honours a 429 retry_after bounded by telegram.retry_after_max; the Telegram token joins the secret sweep. tests/test_telegram.py: 87 checks, 26 red pre-fix.

items.title: lane health tells the truth about a lane that keeps failing
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (2a7d522): lane_down keys the repeat counter on a normalised reason class (a varying message no longer resets it); the lane record merges per lane under the lock (proven with two real processes - a lane this process does not own survives); the poll-failure stamp is monotonic-safe (a backwards clock reports, not hides); _lane_error_permanent requires the HTTP status shape (an id/port containing 401 is not a refused credential); a negative failure count is clamped before the backoff curve; a stale 'up' record is corrected on the exit path and lanes_snapshot can say the pid is dead. the uptime half was refuted by measurement (the clamp is behaviour-preserving); the negative-COUNT half was real and is fixed. tests/test_lane_health.py + test_telegram.py: 23 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: the Telegram lane can carry a file and report its own work
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (2a7d522): sendDocument/sendPhoto appear nowhere in the shipped build, so 'send me the report' returned a Windows path - the transport exists now and run_telegram passes send_file_cb into the run; and a Telegram-only box wires SCHEDULER.dispatcher / REPORTER and honours announce_startup, so a scheduled job reports somewhere and a restart says it is back on this lane too. tests/test_telegram.py: 13 checks red pre-fix.

items.title: the page's door speaks HTTP/1.1, and an answer belongs to its conversation
items.detail: Fixed 2026-10-06 (a065fe5): HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive (every route Content-Length-framed; an undrained body can no longer poison the next request on the socket); HEAD runs the routing and drops the body (curl -I /api/health used to read 501); OPTIONS/PUT/DELETE/PATCH refuse in JSON with Allow; a non-object JSON body answers a JSON 400 instead of raising and closing with zero bytes. The steer door (HIGH): `/api/steer` compares the caller with the run's owning client, so a second tab, a LAN peer or a stale script can no longer answer another conversation's parked question - or the confirm gate. The mutate half of the session registry is scoped to the owning client (a foreign delete removed the runlog file); the shared ?all=1 view keeps working with an explicit title; a pruned conversation's runlog is deleted with it; WebRun.answered is a real latch; a timed-out question draws a line. tests/test_webui.py: 50 checks red pre-fix; keep-alive and HEAD verified live with curl.

items.title: ten fixes: the scheduler, the chat lanes and the app
items.detail: Ten commits (4bc31b3, 0d346d6, 2c8450c, 7499573, 6899f26, 1bdee53, 9f21a34, 46c70af, aa5516a, 9939ccd), each with the regression test that grades it. Sessions and schedule: `_fire` claims the job name under the scheduler's lock, so a job that takes longer than its interval no longer runs several times over on one session key; only a process holding the state lock fires the folder's cron jobs, so a CLI session alive across a boundary no longer steals a due job, prints its answer to a terminal and advances `next`; `add` and `remove` agree on one name, so the name typed is the name removed and re-adding cannot silently overwrite; a job created where there is no reporting channel says its answer goes to the log only. Mattermost: the streamed draft's post id lives on the destination that owns it, so two runs in one channel no longer edit each other's posts; one open question per channel, so a second prompt no longer drops the first; a long answer is cut on a line and never inside an open code fence; a post the server refuses logs the text it lost. TUI: `--app` starts on the 16-colour tier (a `selection_bg` that is not a colour no longer poisons `Style.from_dict`); Ctrl-W gives the pane its columns back. Every fix landed with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix build (`TINYCMDR_SRC`) and the full gate green after each. Also refuted while working: the UTF-16 post-limit premise, the web conversation registry read as a lost update, and a missing tool argument raising out of the door.

items.title: ten fixes: the scheduler, the page, the guards, the a2a and the install door
items.detail: Ten commits, each with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix build and the full gate green after each. Scheduler: a tick's save applies its own delta to jobs.json read under the file lock, so a `--once` add landing between the reload and the save is no longer overwritten (276 of 1989 concurrent adds were lost before); a scheduled job's ask_user row is filed where the Mattermost listener reads answers, so the operator's reply reaches the job instead of starting a new run while the job carries on with its own judgment. Web door: per-request handler state is reset per request, so a refusal after an earlier GET no longer desyncs a kept-alive connection (the third request answered 501); `attach()` refuses a directory, whose download was a Content-Length with no body; `_file` opens the path before it sends headers for the same reason; the conversation registry's `open` map is bounded and drops entries whose conversation is gone. Guards: `_is_mutation` no longer reads a gate refusal as a change, so a refused write cannot wipe the dedupe and loop counters (a model re-issuing one refused write used the whole step budget and the report claimed a write that never happened). a2a: ListTasks answers -32602 for a non-numeric pageSize instead of raising out of the handler. Install and update: install.sh keeps the installer's own exit code (a failed install reported success); the host-owned dir rule is one rule in all six copies, with update.sh/update.ps1 carrying snapshots/ and tmp/ and the parity check parsing every copy.

items.title: a damaged jobs.json is quarantined, and a sessions/ sidecar is not a conversation
items.detail: Two state-file fixes, each with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix build. `jobs.json` was the one state file whose reader answered {} for anything it could not parse - no log line, no `.damaged-*` copy - and `_save` re-read the same way, so a corrupt or transiently-locked file lost the schedule with no evidence anywhere; it routes through the shared `_load_json_state`, a valid-but-non-object file is named too, and tests/test_state_damage.py now covers the fourth state path. The session reload excluded only `.carry.json`, so `.hints.json` and `.question.json` loaded as phantom conversations - and because the hints file IS a JSON list, `tinycmdr sessions` listed one too; `_is_session_file()` answers for the reload and the listing now, while search_sessions keeps tolerating sidecar content on purpose. The `atomic_write_text` docstring, whose opening clause was lost, is restored from the original wording.

items.title: eighteen fixes: the updaters, the spill index, the prompt surface and the shipped docs
items.detail: Eighteen fix commits from three audit runs, each with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix build, and the full gate (106 suites, 0 skipped) green on the batch. Updaters: the page token no longer merges into the last .env line (update.sh's own guard plus update.ps1's read-modify-write), the unix updater prints the file count it always computed, and update.sh takes TINYCMDR_UPDATE_URL so tests/test_update_script.py can serve a fake release over loopback and run the real script end to end. Storage: the spill index's read-merge-write holds the inter-process lock around the READ too, not only the write. Prompt surface: the static prompt names all three things that can move it (a skill, a repo-rules file, a tool built mid-run) and logs a move with its size delta; envelope_line's "remaining" and _compact share one deduction; a sub-agent is no longer told about a custom-tool list its prompt does not carry; a cut AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md block is marked, cut on a line boundary and logged, and a file the budget never reached is named as not read; a Python comment that had been shipping as prompt text is gone, with a gate that refuses the class; skills_index_max_chars is documented in DEFAULT_CONFIG and the shipped example with what 0 means. Docs: README's chars-per-tool figure is graded against the scale gate, and the generated skills/README.md says a skill is per-host and how to share one. Release path: the two-repo split left release.sh publishing into whichever repository `gh` resolved from this tree - the SOURCE, where no installer looks; it now names the install surface explicitly, tags this tree as well (the ledger's anchors are checked against that tag), publishes the generated product tree beside the release, and tests/test_contracts.py grades that the repo a release goes to is the repo the update path and both installers download from.

items.title: every shipped suite is graded on Windows
items.detail: Repointed 2026-10-08. The tier now lives in one file (tests/windows-tier.json), read by tests/run_all.py --tier and named by both workflows, and the exclusions came OFF it: eight suites had been hidden from the Windows job by name, which was the fix for a public job that had been red for weeks and is not a fix. What Windows does in those areas was therefore ungraded, not known-broken - seven of the eight assume a POSIX platform (os.X_OK / os.access / os.chmod / st_mode, a POSIX shell, latin-1, a line console) and test_compaction_continuity carries no platform call at all. Each is red on Windows now and passes on its own commit: fix the suite's platform assumption, or the product where the platform is not the problem. The item closes when the Windows job is green with nothing excluded.
items.gate: make each of the eight pass on Windows (the suite's assumption, or the product), one commit each - the item closes when `excluded` is empty and the Windows job is green

items.title: seventeen fixes: the one-shot door, the lane state, the config verbs and the release path
items.detail: Eleven fixes from two audit runs plus the release-path and CI work they exposed, each with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix build and the full gate (106 suites, 0 skipped) green on the batch. The one-shot door: --once returns 1 when the run never reached the model (the a2a lane's own infra_failed verdict) instead of 0, refuses an empty task, and keeps flags out of the prompt; the console and --app name a missing config.json. Lane state: a record whose writer is gone reads `stale`, never `up`, and health names the dead pid and the record's age. The config verbs: set/unset seed a config.json from the shipped example on a box that has none, get answers from the example without writing, a key nothing reads is refused with the nearest real key named (the known names are derived from the defaults, the example and the code's own reads, so a key the harness really reads is never refused), and a boolean for a string key - which crashed the next start - is refused too. Startup: a headless failed start no longer sleeps 30s, and the page is raised only after validation and the instance lock. The loop: the footer counts discarded attempts (window in, clamped out, with clamped answers named separately) and a tool result that arrives after a later block is attached to its call instead of orphaned beside a fabricated placeholder. Release path: release.sh publishes where installers fetch from and waits for that repository's own workflow, this tree's tag is what the ledger's anchors are checked against, the leak scan refuses a tree that is not a git work tree, the gate hides the harness's own token variables (it was grading the operator's shell), and the install surface's Windows job runs every shipped suite minus eleven named ones, with STATUS.json and a contract check keeping the two lists in step.

items.title: the Windows gate grades everything again, and three cost-guard defects
items.detail: The eight suites hidden from the Windows job are graded there again and each one is fixed rather than listed: two were real Windows defects in the product (the command tokenizer ate every backslash, so a delete of a real document was measured as nothing and asked nothing; the file ledger rendered a path with a mixed separator and the casefolded identity key), one was a tool crashing on a console that cannot carry the glyph it was refusing, and five were suites assuming POSIX (an in-memory console for --app, both platform symbols in the firewall emulation, the documented OSError on the lock probe, the platform restored under an off-Windows assertion, permission bits and separators graded in Windows' own terms). The atomic-claim race check is deterministic now instead of racing the scheduler. From the audit record: the cost guard could not see a bundled short flag (`grep -rn`, `findstr /s`), one level under a user tree was judged the whole profile on macOS but not on Linux, and the elided-call map kept a session per delegation. The runner also stopped reporting a suite that finished as one that died. Three more the first pass exposed: three doors that ask questions (setup, model setup, and the endpoint report's offer to set it up now) got tracebacks instead of their own sentences when stdin reported a tty it could not answer (the Windows NUL device does), an empty host read as this machine because getaddrinfo("") succeeds on Windows, and the ledger's grouping assertion now uses the platform's separator. Two more from the same sweep: a Windows box with nothing running reported "unknown" rather than "not running", because the lock probe never creates the file it reads; and the three question-asking doors each said their own piece instead of tracing back. The gate itself failed one pass with no failure list at all: its own report printed a glyph a Windows console cannot encode, so its streams are hardened like the harness's. The app suite ran on Windows for the first time and three of its checks graded POSIX spellings (the card's rule glyph, a socket census that counts asyncio's AF_INET wakeup there, POSIX mode bits); each asserts its claim where it lives now.
items.gate: the Windows job green on the eight, tests/test_cost_guard.py and tests/test_stall.py green for the three audit fixes

items.title: the two gate inversions: a refusal cannot approve, and a wrapper is not a verb
items.detail: Two gate inversions the whole-harness review found, each with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix build. The confirm gate's answer parser read the whole sentence for a scope word but only its first word for a no, and 'never' meant 'always' there, so a refusal phrased as a sentence ('please never run that') approved the command and wrote the permanent allow-all; a refusal word anywhere is a no now, and an answer that mixes yes and no fails closed. Every guard read a segment's first token as the command's verb, so any wrapper or prefix it did not know (sudo, nice, env X=1, LC_ALL=C, a subshell, then, cmd /c, Start-Process) hid the real command and 19 measured spellings - wipefs, dd of=, mkfs, rm -rf / and whole-tree deletes - ran ungated; one unwrap rule peels wrappers (with the values their switches take), shell keywords, assignments and interpreter payloads for the never tier, the delete rule and the alias arm.
items.gate: tests/test_guard_battery.py red on the pre-fix build and green on the batch; the full gate green

items.title: a parked question reaches the payload, and the index flags are never frozen
items.detail: Four findings from the whole-harness review's second batch, each with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix build. The run loop's budget measurement read the sidecar of a question an unanswered ask_user run had parked and consumed it before any payload was built, so the question never reached the next run at all; the same sidecar survived /new, which would have let it ride a conversation the operator had just abandoned. The measurement now weighs the line without taking delivery (open_question consume=False), the payload build consumes it, and reset clears it. The prompt carried index.md as last written, so a concept whose stale_after instant passed while the bundle was otherwise quiet kept riding every prompt with no (stale) flag - the prompt now renders the index from the concepts at prompt time, and the file stays the mutation-written browse copy for humans and the other consumers. The add path rendered that index before deprecating the concept it supersedes, so the superseded entry rode unflagged next to its replacement until a later mutation re-rendered.
items.gate: tests/test_ask_user.py and tests/test_memory_okf.py red on the pre-fix build (6 and 3 FAILs) and green on the batch; the full gate green

items.title: six gate holes: continuations, -enc abbreviations, Mac disks, the grant, the store, the allow scope
items.detail: The six findings left in the guard slice after -88, each verified against the code and graded by tests/test_guard_battery.py (30 checks red on the pre-fix build). A backslash (bash) or backtick (PowerShell) line continuation ended one segment at the newline, so `dd bs=1M \<newline>of=/dev/sda`, a backtick-continued `format` and `find / \<newline>-delete` split and the half carrying the target read clean - one join before any guard reads tokens now. The encoded-PowerShell arm matched only exact tokens plus the full word, so -enco/-encod/-encoded and every slash spelling passed it and the shipped blocked_patterns regex; any accepted abbreviation counts now (colon/equals values, en/em dashes). The never tier had no macOS disk verb and missed common Linux ones - diskutil (write subcommands only; list/info stay usable), parted, sfdisk, cfdisk, gdisk, blkdiscard, mkswap, asr and newfs_* are never-tier. A `session` approval lived for the life of the process under a key /new keeps, so a fresh conversation inherited it; reset drops it with the conversation. The confirm gate's own file was writable by the model (write_file, edit_file, a redirect or an open() call) and a permanent grant answered for lanes with nobody to ask: writes to confirm-allow.json are refused on every door now (file doors by resolved path, shell/code in is_blocked), and a no-door lane decides by agent.confirm_without_door and nothing else. items.title: a Windows removal finishes, or names what is left
items.detail: The removal a Windows user runs could end as 'done' with the folder still there: the sweep took one process snapshot and no children (the supervisor respawns the bot, a tool child can hold the folder), and a shell standing in the folder - the natural way to run it - makes the delete impossible on Windows.
